body.title: fix: resolve forgejo-actions users by id
body.body:
**Issue**: The activity feed said "Ghost commented on pull request XYZ". Nobody was deleted. The comment was actually a test-results comment posted by CI, and the pull request page itself showed the author, `forgejo-actions` user, which is not stored as an account. `forgejo-actions` is only created in memory, when needed, in `models/user/user_system.go`.

**Fix**: Make the feed use the lookups that know the built-in users from `user_system.go`:
- LoadActUser: GetPossibleUserByID instead of GetUserByID.
- LoadActUsers: GetPossibleUserByIDs instead of the direct database query.

Deleted accounts still show as Ghost, because their IDs are positive and still aren't found in the table.

I looked up that Gitea fixed the same bug in [go-gitea/gitea#34703](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/34703), backported in [#34756](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/34756), with the same change to LoadActUser. Forgejo hasn't ported it. My PR brings it to forgejo.

body.title: perf: stop loading repo topics twice
body.body:
The repo topics (the user definable labels for a repo) were already loaded and put on the context. There's no need to do it a second time.

This is tested properly, and now arguably in a better way. The test data had topics for repos 1, 2 and 33 in the topics table, but an empty array in the fixtures. This wasn't a problem before because of the extra topic retrieval. As soon as that was removed the tests failed, so now the topics are correctly in the fixtures.

How are they retrieved the first time?
- Every `/{username}/{reponame}/..` goes through [the `context.RepoAssignment` middleware](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/src/commit/1a13355998e2e0183e74d0221e0504564ca21e6c/routers/web/web.go#L1418).
- The `RepoAssignment` loads the repository [here](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/src/branch/forgejo/services/context/repo.go#L533).
- The `GetRepositoryByName` does a query for the entire `repositorry`, which includes `topics`.
